In brief: A low-pressure system is expected to dominate the weather pattern in Abuja over the next week, leading to a significant chance of rainfall on most days, with temperatures ranging from 22°C to 30°C. ### Monday The low-pressure system currently situated over the region is expected to persist, leading to a high likelihood of rainfall, with a 73% chance of precipitation. Temperatures are expected to reach a high of 29°C, while the low will dip to 22°C. The high humidity, currently at 92%, will contribute to the feeling of warmth, making the temperature feel more like 27°C. As the day progresses, the winds will shift from a southeasterly direction to a southwesterly direction, picking up speed to around 15 km/h. This wind shift will lead to an increase in cloud cover, ultimately resulting in the anticipated rainfall. The rainfall accumulation is expected to range from 10 to 20 mm, with the majority of it falling in the late afternoon.
The rainfall is expected to affect various parts of the city differently, with low-lying flood-prone areas such as Gwarinpa and parts of Wuse being more susceptible to flash flooding. Residents in these areas should be cautious and take necessary precautions. In contrast, areas such as Maitama and Asokoro, which are at a higher elevation, are expected to experience less severe flooding. The Abuja airport road may experience some disruptions due to the rainfall, and commuters should plan their travel accordingly. The rainfall is expected to clear up by the evening, leading to a relatively cool night. The temperature will dip to 22°C, and the humidity will decrease slightly, making the night feel more comfortable. The wind will continue to blow from a southwesterly direction, albeit at a slower speed of around 10 km/h.
